# Auto-update test fixture

Two-version CodeTerm rig for end-to-end `update --apply` verification. Pair
this with `tests/e2e/test_update_resume.py`.

## Layout

```
tests/fixtures/auto-update/
├── README.md                  this file
├── manifest.json              local-asset-server manifest (regenerated by build-fixture.sh)
├── build-fixture.sh           builds OLD + NEW signed CodeTerm versions
├── regenerate-manifest.py     inlines real .sig contents into manifest.json
└── dist/                      build outputs (.msi.zip / .app.tar.gz + .sig); gitignored
```

`dist/` starts empty. The committed `manifest.json` carries placeholder
signatures; running `build-fixture.sh` overwrites it with a manifest whose
signatures match the assets that just landed in `dist/`.

## Build the rig

```bash
# from repo root
./tests/fixtures/auto-update/build-fixture.sh
```

Produces (Windows host):

```
dist/codeterm-0.0.1-test-x64.msi.zip
dist/codeterm-0.0.1-test-x64.msi.zip.sig
dist/codeterm-0.0.2-test-x64.msi.zip
dist/codeterm-0.0.2-test-x64.msi.zip.sig
manifest.json   ← regenerated, points at NEW (0.0.2-test) asset
```

macOS host substitutes `.app.tar.gz` and writes the matching architecture
key (`darwin-aarch64` or `darwin-x86_64`).

Override versions via env:

```bash
FIXTURE_OLD_VERSION=0.0.7-test \
FIXTURE_NEW_VERSION=0.0.8-test \
    ./tests/fixtures/auto-update/build-fixture.sh
```

## Serve assets

```bash
cd tests/fixtures/auto-update
python3 -m http.server 8080
```

The manifest URL becomes `http://127.0.0.1:8080/manifest.json` and asset
URLs resolve to `http://127.0.0.1:8080/dist/<file>`. The backend only
accepts loopback HTTP when built with `--features dev-updater-allowlocal`
(see `src-tauri/src/update/manifest.rs`).

## Apply against a running OLD-version CodeTerm

Install the OLD `.msi`/`.app` first, launch it, then trigger the update:

```bash
codeterm update --apply --manifest-url http://127.0.0.1:8080/manifest.json
```

The CLI proxies the manifest URL to the REST `/api/update/install` endpoint
(`cli/src/main.rs` `Update { manifest_url, ... }`). The backend hands the
override to `tauri-plugin-updater`, downloads the NEW asset, verifies the
ed25519 signature, runs the SHUTDOWN PRELUDE, swaps the binary, and
relaunches.

## Drive the e2e test

```bash
export CODETERM_RUN_UPDATE_RESUME=1
export CODETERM_TEST_MANIFEST_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8080/manifest.json
pytest tests/e2e/test_update_resume.py -v
```

Without those env vars the survival test is `SKIPPED` — the snapshot-shape
check still runs to catch tab-payload regressions.

## Re-key

When the dev signing keypair rotates, regenerate the embedded pubkey in
`src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` (see
[essences/contributing/auto-update-signing.md](../../../essences/contributing/auto-update-signing.md))
and rebuild both versions — the OLD installed binary must trust the new
key or the apply step will reject the manifest.
